bumbleinc-bumbleinc:lever:1471617a-d0fc-.title: Associate Director, FP&A
bumbleinc-bumbleinc:lever:1471617a-d0fc-.description: At Bumble, we’re building the Love Company — creating products and experiences that help people form healthy, equitable relationships and friendships. This role sits at the heart of how we invest in growth: you’ll partner closely with Marketing to translate bold ideas into clear plans, smart trade-offs, and measurable outcomes. You’ll bring Curiosity and Courage to complex decisions, pairing sharp commercial judgement with respectful, people-first partnering. With a strong FP&A team around you, you’ll help raise the bar on how we forecast, learn, and act — using AI thoughtfully to move faster while keeping the work grounded in sound governance and human insight.

cogentanalytics-cogentanalytics:lever:96.title: Warehouse Clerk
cogentanalytics-cogentanalytics:lever:96.description: About the Role The Warehouse Clerk is responsible for the day-to-day management of the warehouse, yard, equipment, tools, materials, and vehicle fleet. This role serves as the primary point of accountability for all inventory and company assets, ensuring everything that enters, leaves, or moves within company locations is accurately tracked and documented. The Warehouse Clerk maintains organized inventory systems that support field operations and ensure crews have the materials and equipment they need to complete projects efficiently. Key Responsibilities Manage all warehouse and yard operations, ensuring materials, tools, equipment, and vehicles are properly logged, tracked, and accounted for. Pick, stage, and prepare materials, tools, and supplies for field crews before scheduled work assignments. Maintain inventory using established minimum/maximum stock levels and proactively replenish inventory to prevent shortages and project delays. Receive incoming materials, equipment, and supplies, ensuring all receiving and inventory transactions are accurately recorded in the company's accounting or inventory management system. Coordinate preventive maintenance and repair schedules for company vehicles, trailers, tools, and equipment, including inspections, registrations, and routine service. Maintain a clean, organized, and secure warehouse and yard environment. Track equipment and vehicle assignments to projects and crews, ensuring all assets are returned, inspected, and documented after use. Maintain accurate records of inventory counts, equipment condition, maintenance history, and asset locations. Identify low inventory levels, aging equipment, damaged tools, or maintenance needs before they impact project schedules. Enforce company procedures for inventory control and asset accountability by ensuring all employees follow established check-in/check-out processes. Assist with periodic physical inventory counts and inventory reconciliations.

jobgether-jobgether:lever:0fc49714-d5a3-.title: Lead Site Reliability Engineer - Imunify Reliability Platform
jobgether-jobgether:lever:0fc49714-d5a3-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Lead Site Reliability Engineer - Imunify Reliability Platform based in Finland. This is a greenfield SRE leadership opportunity within a large-scale, security-focused product environment. You will define what “healthy” means across roughly 70 components spanning cloud services and customer-hosted agents. You will establish SLIs, SLOs, error budgets, monitoring standards, alerting, and escalation practices from the ground up. Your work will directly improve the ability to detect silent security-control degradation before it becomes a widespread customer-impacting issue. You will collaborate closely with engineering leads and senior engineers while building the telemetry and reliability platform yourself. The environment is remote-first, async, technically demanding, and focused on measurable outcomes rather than dashboards for their own sake. This is an opportunity to shape the reliability culture and foundations of a major security product. Define and establish meaningful SLIs for approximately 70 product components, working with squad leads and senior engineers to agree on ownership, measurement, tiering, SLOs, and error budgets. Develop a reliability taxonomy covering service availability and latency, fleet reachability and configuration convergence, security-control efficacy, artifact delivery, and telemetry pipeline health. Ensure reliability indicators are independently measurable and cannot be disabled by the same failure they are intended to detect. Design and build the telemetry collection pipeline for customer-hosted agents and cloud services, balancing push-based collection, sampling, privacy constraints, data quality, and cardinality. Extend instrumentation across Python, Go, and Rust components in collaboration with product engineering teams. Consolidate existing dashboards, queries, and reporting mechanisms into a smaller, more reliable observability platform, retiring tooling that does not provide meaningful operational value. Implement symptom-based, SLO-driven alerting with multi-window burn-rate principles and clear page, ticket, and dashboard classifications. Ensure every production alert has a defined owner, documented failure mode, and actionable runbook. Establish ongoing alert-quality practices, including periodic reviews, measurable actionable-alert rates, and deliberate removal of unnecessary alerts. Build a machine-readable ownership and escalation model that routes incidents to the appropriate engineering squads. Establish severity definitions, acknowledgement expectations, follow-the-sun escalation practices, and clean handoff procedures across multiple time zones. Strengthen incident command and blameless postmortem practices, including reliable timelines, ownership, and follow-through on corrective actions. Coach engineering squads to own their own operational responsibilities and paging rather than becoming a centralized buffer for other teams' alerts. Deliver measurable reliability outcomes over the first year, including complete SLI ownership, production telemetry, tiered alerting, squad on-call adoption, and a significant reduction in the time required to detect silent security-control degradation. Requirements Substantial production engineering or SRE experience, including experience defining and implementing an SLO framework rather than simply operating within an existing one. Strong Python skills and the ability to read and modify Go or Rust code when implementing instrumentation and reliability improvements. Strong hands-on experience with time-series and event telemetry at scale, including Prometheus/OpenMetrics, Grafana, Alertmanager-class routing systems, and columnar or high-cardinality data stores such as ClickHouse or equivalent technologies. Experience debugging distributed systems running on bare metal and long-lived hosts; this role requires more than Ku

jobgether-jobgether:lever:422c1ed0-8ed7-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Director, Legal based in the United States. This is a highly visible opportunity to build and lead the legal function for a fast-growing, privacy-first healthcare technology business. As the first in-house counsel, you will serve as a strategic partner to the CEO and leadership team across commercial, privacy, compliance, corporate, employment, and product matters. You will work directly within the business and deal cycle, helping teams move quickly while managing legal and regulatory risk thoughtfully. The role combines hands-on commercial contracting with privacy-by-design guidance for products and technology handling sensitive healthcare data. You will establish scalable legal processes, playbooks, and frameworks that enable the organization to grow efficiently without unnecessary friction. The environment is entrepreneurial, fast-moving, and highly autonomous, with significant opportunity to shape how the business approaches legal strategy and risk. This role is ideal for a pragmatic legal leader who brings strong judgment, clear communication, and a business-oriented approach to complex technology and privacy challenges. Build the legal function: Establish and lead the in-house legal function, developing scalable processes, workflows, templates, and practices that support a growing technology organization. Commercial contracting: Own commercial agreements end to end across new business, renewals, expansions, partner and agency relationships, and technology and data partnerships. Contracting infrastructure: Develop practical contract templates, negotiation playbooks, and workflows that enable business teams to move efficiently while reducing unnecessary legal friction. Privacy-by-design: Partner closely with Product and Engineering from the earliest stages of development to embed privacy considerations into product and technology decisions rather than treating them as late-stage reviews. Privacy and compliance: Advise leadership and cross-functional teams on data privacy, data protection, security, healthcare-related regulations, and other compliance requirements relevant to products and operations. Strategic risk management: Serve as a trusted advisor to the CEO and senior leaders, translating legal risks into practical options that allow the business to pursue opportunities safely and effectively. Corporate legal matters: Support corporate governance, financing, equity, employment, intellectual property, and other legal matters as the organization evolves. Outside counsel: Manage external legal advisors and legal spend strategically, ensuring outside resources are used effectively. Cross-functional partnership: Collaborate closely with executive leadership and teams across Product, Engineering, Sales, and other functions to provide timely, commercially minded legal guidance. Organizational scalability: Develop a proactive, business-first approach to legal operations and risk management that can scale alongside the company's growth. Requirements Legal credentials: Juris Doctor (J.D.) degree and active membership in at least one U.S. state bar. In-house experience: Demonstrated in-house legal experience within a technology or SaaS company, ideally in an earlier-stage, high-growth startup environment. Commercial expertise: Strong experience negotiating, structuring, and managing commercial agreements throughout the customer and vendor lifecycle. Privacy and technology law: Deep familiarity with privacy, data protection, technology transactions, and related regulatory considerations; healthcare regulatory experience is strongly preferred. Business judgment: Ability to balance appropriate legal and regulatory risk management with commercial priorities, customer needs, speed, and business objectives. jobgether-jobgether:lever:c6e2f54e-de09-.description: This position is listed on behalf of a partner company, who manages all applications and next steps. Our partner is looking for a Staff Software Engineer, Backend based in Switzerland. This is a high-impact backend engineering role focused on building and scaling developer infrastructure that powers integrations between applications and the real world. You will own critical backend systems, APIs, and services from initial concept through production and ongoing improvement. The role offers significant influence over technical direction, product strategy, and the evolution of the developer experience. You will work closely with developer customers to understand integration challenges and turn them into practical, scalable solutions. As a senior technical contributor, you will help drive performance, reliability, scalability, and engineering quality across the platform. You will also contribute to open-source development and collaborate with a highly autonomous, distributed engineering team. This opportunity is ideal for an experienced backend engineer who combines deep technical expertise with strong product judgment and developer empathy. Design, build, and scale backend systems, APIs, and services that support a developer-focused integration platform. Develop high-quality developer interfaces, including APIs, SDKs, user interfaces, and backend runtimes that deliver an excellent developer experience. Own critical engineering initiatives end-to-end, from ideation and technical design through implementation, deployment, and continuous improvement. Collaborate directly with developer customers to understand integration challenges, troubleshoot complex issues, and translate feedback into product improvements. Optimize backend services for performance, scalability, reliability, and operational resilience as usage grows. Influence the technical roadmap and broader product strategy through strong ownership of architectural and engineering decisions. Contribute to and maintain open-source projects, engaging with the developer community and improving the platform based on real-world needs. Provide technical leadership through thoughtful design decisions, pragmatic problem-solving, incident participation, and support for other engineers. Help shape engineering practices and standards while maintaining a strong focus on developer experience and product outcomes. Requirements 10+ years of backend software engineering experience for a Staff-level position, with a demonstrated ability to build and scale high-traffic production systems. Deep expertise in backend engineering, developer infrastructure, APIs, databases, and performance-critical systems. Pragmatic, positive, and low-ego approach to teamwork, including a willingness to step in during incidents and help unblock colleagues.
